# Capture demo requests: HubSpot for routing

**Pattern:** Lead Capture & Routing · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Form

## Overview

Starts when the form is submitted, and covers routing work end to end across HubSpot, Gmail and Slack.

It moves through 17 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. New Lead Form Submission
2. Normalize Lead Payload
3. Route by Work Type
4. Process 'mql' → HubSpot
5. Fast-Track 'sql' + Alert
6. Hold Unknown Types (DLQ)
7. Merge Routed Work
8. Cap Batch Volume
9. Stamp Processing Time
10. Align Field Names
11. Sort Leads Newest First
12. Save Execution Metadata
13. Guard Non-Empty email
14. Tag Pipeline Metadata
15. Summarize Run Stats
16. Append Audit Row (HubSpot)
17. Send Summary to Gmail

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing routing work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

New Lead Form Submission → Normalize Lead Payload → Route by Work Type → Process 'mql' → HubSpot → Fast-Track 'sql' + Alert → Hold Unknown Types (DLQ) → Merge Routed Work → Cap Batch Volume → Stamp Processing Time → Align Field Names → Sort Leads Newest First → Save Execution Metadata → Guard Non-Empty email → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (HubSpot) → Send Summary to Gmail → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack

## Use it for

- Teams keeping HubSpot and Gmail aligned by hand for routing
- Intake checked for completeness before it is stored in HubSpot, for routing
- Routing work where "Normalize Lead Payload" is still a manual step before HubSpot
- Routing work that only reaches HubSpot when a form is submitted, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps HubSpot and Gmail in step for routing, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed HubSpot or Gmail call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 19 nodes in this routing build
- Branches rejoin before HubSpot, so a routing run reports once rather than 19 times
- Every routing run leaves an audit row behind, alongside HubSpot
- Fans the same result out to Slack in the same run, for routing

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Google OAuth2; HubSpot private-app token; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Unrecognized work types are parked in a dead-letter lane instead of erroring the whole run or silently dropping the item — new event kinds will show up eventually, and this is where you'd notice one without losing it. One kind is deliberately routed through a sub-workflow to show how heavier per-type logic can be extracted without touching this router at all.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Send a work-type value that matches no switch rule and confirm it lands in the dead-letter branch.
2. Add a new work type and its own handling branch.
3. Replace the direct-write branch with a sub-workflow call, matching the pattern already used for the first kind.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**HubSpot private-app token**
HubSpot → Settings → Integrations → Private Apps → create app → copy the token.
_Gotcha:_ Grant the CRM scopes you need; legacy API keys are deprecated and will not work.

**Google OAuth2**
Google Cloud Console → enable Gmail API → OAuth consent screen → OAuth client ID (Web).
_Gotcha:_ Add n8n's OAuth redirect URL exactly as shown in the credential, or the consent loop fails.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your routing process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- HubSpot: a private-app token carrying only the CRM scopes these nodes use — legacy API keys are deprecated and over-broad.
- Gmail: request the narrowest send/read scope the nodes need — full mailbox access is rarely required.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.

**Do not log**
routing payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
